paragraphs.text: ונסבו להון נשין כל חד וחד מנהון אתבחר לה אנתה ושריו למעלה עליהן ולסאבה עמהן ואלפו אנון חרשין ולחרסה ולקטיעת שרשין ועקרין ואחויו להון עשבין
paragraphs.translit: wa-něsabū lěhōn něšīn kol ḥad wĕ-ḥad minhōn ʾitběḥar leh ʾinttāh wĕ-šārīw lě-meʿlāh ʿălēhēn wĕ-lě-saʾāḇāh ʿimhēn wa-ʾallēpū ʾinnōn ḥăršīn wĕ-lě-ḥāršāh wĕ-lě-qěṭīʿat šoršīn wĕ-ʿiqqārīn wĕ-ʾaḥwīw lěhōn ʿiśbīn

i18n.en: And they took to themselves wives, and each one chose for himself a wife; and they began to go in unto them and to defile themselves with them. And they taught them sorceries and enchantments and the cutting of roots, and made them acquainted with plants.

paragraphs.commentary: The Watchers take human wives and teach them magic and pharmacology — the convergence of the *bĕnê ʾĕlōhîm*-narrative of Gen 6:1-4 with the apkallū-tradition of forbidden-knowledge-transfer. See central entry `nephilim-giants-1-enoch-7-gen-6-4-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: ואלין הריון מנהון וילדו גברי רברבין רומהון תלת מאה אמין
paragraphs.translit: wĕ-ʾillēn hărīyōn minhōn wĕ-yělidū gibbārīn rabrěbīn rūmhōn tělāt měʾāh ʾammīn

i18n.en: And these conceived from them, and bore great giants, whose height was three hundred cubits.

paragraphs.commentary: **The 300-vs-3000-cubits giant-stature textual-variant.** The Aramaic 4Q201 fragment (where reconstructable) appears to read 300 cubits; the Greek Akhmim and Ge'ez read 3000 cubits — a 10-fold textual-variant that has been extensively discussed (Milik 1976 takes 300 as original; Nickelsburg 2001 documents the dispute). See per-translation overlay `300-vs-3000-cubits-giant-height-variant-1-enoch-7-2-witness-variant`. The cubit-figures are theological-mythological exaggeration in the apocalyptic-narrative register, not measurements of any physical entity; popular-fringe gigantism readings are not source-textually warranted.

paragraphs.text: οὗτοι κατήσθιον τοὺς κόπους τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὡς δὲ οὐχ ὑπέφερον αὐτοὺς τρέφειν οἱ ἄνθρωποι,
paragraphs.translit: houtoi katēsthion tous kopous tōn anthrōpōn, hōs de ouch hypepheron autous trephein hoi anthrōpoi,

i18n.en: These devoured the labor of mankind; and when men could no longer sustain them,

paragraphs.text: ἐπεστράφησαν οἱ γίγαντες κατὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὥστε κατεσθίειν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: epestraphēsan hoi gigantes kata tōn anthrōpōn, hōste katesthiein autous.

i18n.en: the giants turned against them and devoured mankind.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἁμαρτάνειν ἐν τοῖς πετεινοῖς καὶ τοῖς θηρίοις καὶ τοῖς ἑρπετοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἰχθύσιν, καὶ ἀλλήλων τὰς σάρκας κατεσθίειν, καὶ τὸ αἷμα ἔπινον.
paragraphs.translit: kai ērxanto hamartanein en tois peteinois kai tois thēriois kai tois herpetois kai tois ichthysin, kai allēlōn tas sarkas katesthiein, kai to haima epinon.

i18n.en: And they began to sin against birds and beasts and reptiles and fish, and to devour one another's flesh, and they drank the blood.

paragraphs.commentary: The giants' consumption of birds, beasts, reptiles, fish — and finally of each other's flesh — is the etiology-of-evil escalation that sets up the demonological framework at 1 En 15:8-12 (the disembodied-spirits-of-the-dead-giants become the evil-spirits). See central entry `giants-become-evil-spirits-demonology-1-enoch-15-cross-corpus-jub-10-tertullian`.

paragraphs.text: τότε ἡ γῆ ἐνέτυχεν κατὰ τῶν ἀνόμων.
paragraphs.translit: tote hē gē enetychen kata tōn anomōn.

i18n.en: Then the earth brought a complaint against the lawless ones.
